hints: Focus on what the dot in ClO• really tells you about its total electron count.
Count the valence electrons: Cl brings 7 and O brings 6, giving 13 in total, which is definitely odd.
Think about how that single Cl-O bond is made, one electron from each atom, and ask if oxygen needed to donate both electrons.
walkthrough:
**Check for odd electrons**

All free radicals have one unpaired electron, so they must have an odd total. Let's count to be sure.

$$\text{valence electrons} = 7(\text{Cl}) + 6(\text{O}) = 13$$

13 is odd, so statement 1 is true.

**Draw the bonding**

Cl needs one more electron to complete its octet, and O in this radical also shares one electron to form one bond.

$$\text{Cl} \cdot + \cdot \text{O} \rightarrow \text{Cl-O} \cdot$$

That is one shared pair, a normal single covalent bond. So statement 2 is true.

**Test for dative bonding**

A dative bond means one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair. Here each atom contributed one electron, just like a normal covalent bond.

So there is no donation from oxygen to chlorine, and statement 3 is false.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1 and 2 are true, statement 3 is false. That combination matches 1 and 2 only.

options.A: This suggests 1, 2 and 3 are all true. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong because the Cl-O bond is a normal shared pair, not a dative donation from O to Cl.
options.B: This is 1 and 2 only, which is correct. ClO• has 13 valence electrons (odd), and it contains one normal single covalent Cl-O bond with an unpaired electron left on oxygen.
options.C: This suggests 2 and 3 only. It wrongly leaves out statement 1 (all radicals have an odd electron count) and wrongly includes statement 3 (there is no dative bond here).
options.D: This suggests 1 only. While 1 is true, it misses statement 2. The radical clearly has one Cl-O single bond holding the two atoms together.
